The sample proportion who agree is 466/1012 ≈ 46%. With a 3% margin of error, the 95% confidence interval is 43% to 49%.

The statement misreads what that interval means. The interval is built around this one sample's proportion. Sample proportions from repeated samples would instead centre on the true population proportion, which we don't know. So 95% of them would fall within about 3% of the true value, not necessarily between 43% and 49%. The 95% describes how often the method captures the true proportion, not the share of sample proportions that land in this particular range.

The statement is false.

ANSWER: false
